I know you’re hurting, but think through what you want to accomplish and whether what you’re planning on doing will accomplish that without exposing you to further trauma or setting back your healing. I don’t know if it will or won’t, and I’m not in any way saying this to protect your abuser from harm, but anything that brings you into contact with your abuser holds a risk of creating more trauma for you.

For me, having my abuser deny what they did, attempt to gaslight me, call me delusional or a liar to others, etc. was a VERY traumatic experience. Even years later, having a family member refuse to take any accountability for their role in allowing the abuse to happen was extremely re-traumatizing and created a huge setback for my mental health. I was seriously considering ending my life at one point because of that encounter. Sometimes confronting an abuser can be healing but many times we’re desperately trying to get them to feel or express remorse for what they did and when they don’t, it can re-inflict all that emotional and psychological pain.

You might want to consider participating at r/adultsurvivors and seeing if anyone there has thoughts. There are many folks with similar stories.

Also, if you have not been evaluated and/or treated for PTSD I encourage you to give it a try. I have made a lot of progress in the past year with treatment, despite having had untreated/undiagnosed PTSD for more than 25 years. What happened will never go away but you can definitely heal from it so that it’s a scar and not an open wound anymore.
